properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 27 at 9:34PM PDT until October 29 at 1:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:

* WHERE...San Diego County coastal areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...Until 1 PM PDT Thursday during high tides in the late
mornings.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur in the
late mornings.

infrastructure in the warned area should prepare for rising
water and take appropriate action to protect life and
property. High tides each day will occur in the late morning.

tide predictions.
properties.instruction:

travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

properties.areaDesc: Bent, CO
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 27 at 8:52PM MDT until October 29 at 2:00AM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Colorado...

Purgatoire River Near Las Animas affecting Bent County.

For the Purgatoire River...including Las Animas...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...High flow is traveling down the Upper Purgatoire from recent
rains, and may lead to flooding near Las Animas.

* WHERE...Purgatoire River near Las Animas.

* WHEN...Until late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Minor Flood. Minor agricultural flooding
occurs into low lying areas along the river.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 PM MDT Tuesday the stage was 9.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:15 PM MDT Tuesday was 9.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 9.7 feet
tomorrow morning. It will then fall below flood stage early
tomorrow afternoon.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 9.8
feet on 06/06/1949.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday morning at 900 AM MDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL LATE WEDNESDAY NIGHT

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Georgetown
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 27 at 10:31PM EDT until October 28 at 12:00PM EDT by NWS Wilmington NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to one foot of
inundation above ground level expected in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Georgetown County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 8 AM to noon EDT
Wednesday. For the High Rip Current Risk, from 8 AM EDT
Wednesday through Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Vulnerable causeways to and from local beaches will
experience minor coastal flooding. Low-lying roads and
locations along the Intracoastal Waterway and adjacent tidal
creeks will observe minor coastal flooding. Check with local
officials for the latest information regarding coastal flood
impacts and closures. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Affected areas listed are based on
average tide conditions. Additional locations may experience
flooding during periods of heavy rainfall, high winds, or
other factors.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a Flood
Advisory for the following rivers in New Mexico...

Rio Grande at Embudo affecting Rio Arriba and Taos Counties.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Embudo.

* WHEN...From this evening to Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Minor overbank flows are occurring above the
Embudo gaging site. Access to riverside picnic facilities above
Pilar and below the Taos Junction Bridge along State Route 570 will
be limited if further rises occur. Water may be extremely close to
underside of bridge over Rio Grande on Aguas Caliente Rd in Pilar.

expected until the river rises to 12 feet.

- Bankfull stage is 8.0 feet.

- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

alternative route.

properties.areaDesc: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Mayaguez and Vicinity
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 27 at 9:27PM AST until October 28 at 2:00AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to
10 feet. For the HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK, life-threatening rip
current.

* WHERE... For the HIGH SURF ADVISORY, the most vulnerable areas
for high surf and beach erosion include Pinones along Road 187,
Parcelas Suarez, Villas del Mar, and Villa Christiana in Loiza;
Fortuna in Luquillo; Pueblo and Tamarindo in Aguadilla; Bario
Obrero, Pueblo and Jareaito in Arecibo; Las Boca in Barceloneta;
Machuca in Manati; Puerto Nuevo in Vega Baja; Ocean Park in San
Juan; and Barrio Espinal in Aguada. For the HIGH RIP CURRENT
RISK, beaches along west to northeast Puerto Rico.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory remains until 2 AM AST
Wednesday. For the High Rip Current Risk remains through Wednesday
afternoon.

* IMPACTS...FOR THE HIGH SURF ADVISORY, High waves that can wash
over jetties and sweep people and pets onto jagged rocks.
Rough surf may also knock you down. Large breaking waves will
result in localized beach/dune structure erosion and dangerous
swimming conditions. FOR THE HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK, rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water, where it becomes difficult to return to safety.
properties.instruction:
A High Surf Advisory means that high surf will affect beaches in
the advisory area, producing localized beach erosion and
dangerous swimming conditions.

There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

A High Surf Advisory means that high surf will affect beaches in
the advisory area, producing localized beach erosion and
dangerous swimming conditions.
